title: Kanglexin counters vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation and associated arteriosclerosis through inhibiting PDGFR.
authors: Yang, Shuang; Zhao, Yixiu; Cao, Shifeng; Liu, Xinxin; Feng, Min; Chen, Yi; Ma, Chunyue; Zhan, Tingting; Zhang, Qi; Jia, Honglin; Zhao, Yu; Tong, Ming; Yu, Yuanyuan; Liu, Xue; Yang, Baofeng; Zhang, Yan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物Kanglexin通过PDGFR信号通路抑制血管平滑肌细胞去分化，虽涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysregulation of vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) function leads to a variety of diseases such as atherosclerosis and hyperplasia after injury. However, antiproliferative drug targeting VSMC exhibits poor specificity. Therefore, there is an urgent to develop highly specific antiproliferative drugs to prevention and treatment VSMC dedifferentiation associated arteriosclerosis. Kanglexin (KLX), a new anthraquinone compound designed by our team, has potential to regulate VSMC phenotype according to the physicochemical properties. PURPOSE: This project aims to evaluate the therapeutic role of KLX in VSMC dedifferentiation and atherosclerosis, neointimal formation and illustrates the underlying molecular mechanism. METHODS: In vivo, the ApoE(-/-) mice were fed with high-fat diet (HFD) for a duration of 13 weeks to establish the atherosclerotic model. And rat carotid artery injury model was performed to establish the neointimal formation model. In vitro, PDGF-BB was used to induce VSMC dedifferentiation. RESULTS: We found that KLX ameliorated the atherosclerotic progression including atherosclerotic lesion formation, lipid deposition and collagen deposition in aorta and aortic sinus in atherosclerotic mouse model. In addition, The administration of KLX effectively ameliorated neointimal formation in the carotid artery following balloon injury in SD rats. The findings derived from molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments unequivocally demonstrate that KLX had potential to bind PDGFR-beta. Mechanism research work proved that KLX prevented VSMC proliferation, migration and dedifferentiation via activating the PDGFR-beta-MEK -ERK-ELK-1/KLF4 signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: Collectively, we demonstrated that KLX effectively attenuated the progression of atherosclerosis in ApoE-/- mice and carotid arterial neointimal formation in SD rats by inhibiting VSMC phenotypic conversion via PDGFR-beta-MEK-ERK-ELK-1/KLF4 signaling. KLX exhibits promising potential as a viable therapeutic agent for the treatment of VSMC phenotype conversion associated arteriosclerosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：血管平滑肌细胞（VSMC）功能失调导致多种疾病，如动脉粥样硬化和损伤后增生。然而，靶向VSMC的抗增殖药物特异性较差。因此，迫切需要开发高特异性的抗增殖药物，以预防和治疗与VSMC去分化相关的动脉硬化。康乐欣（KLX）是我们团队设计的一种新型蒽醌类化合物，根据其理化性质，具有调节VSMC表型的潜力。目的：本项目旨在评估KLX在VSMC去分化、动脉粥样硬化和新生内膜形成中的治疗作用，并阐明其潜在分子机制。方法：在体内，ApoE(-/-)小鼠喂食高脂饮食（HFD）13周以建立动脉粥样硬化模型。同时，采用大鼠颈动脉损伤模型建立新生内膜形成模型。在体外，使用PDGF-BB诱导VSMC去分化。结果：我们发现KLX改善了动脉粥样硬化小鼠模型中主动脉和主动脉窦的动脉粥样硬化病变形成、脂质沉积和胶原沉积。此外，KLX给药有效改善了SD大鼠球囊损伤后颈动脉的新生内膜形成。分子对接和表面等离子体共振（SPR）实验的结果明确表明，KLX具有结合PDGFR-β的潜力。机制研究工作证明，KLX通过激活PDGFR-β-MEK-ERK-ELK-1/KLF4信号通路，阻止了VSMC的增殖、迁移和去分化。结论：总体而言，我们证明KLX通过PDGFR-β-MEK-ERK-ELK-1/KLF4信号通路抑制VSMC表型转化，有效减轻了ApoE-/-小鼠动脉粥样硬化的进展和SD大鼠颈动脉新生内膜的形成。KLX作为治疗VSMC表型转化相关动脉硬化的可行治疗药物，展现出良好的潜力。
